question: Chemical change is not-
solution:
The correct answer is **__Boiling of Water__**.

__
 
• A chemical change occurs **when the substance's composition is changed**.
 
• **When bonds are broken and new ones are formed a chemical change occurs**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chemical changes** cause a substance to change into an entire substance with a new chemical formula.

 
 
• Examples of Chemical Change: burned wood becomes ash, carbon dioxide, and water. When exposed to water, iron becomes a mixture of several hydrated iron oxides and hydroxides.
 
 
 
• **Physical changes** only change the appearance of a substance.
 
 
• Physical changes are limited to changes that result in a difference in the display without changing the composition.
 
• **Boiling of water is an example of Physical change**__.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• When** two or more reactants are mixed and a change in temperature, colour, etc. is noticed, a chemical reaction is probably occurring**.

 
 
• A change in colour is not always a chemical change.
 
• If one were to change the colour of a substance in a non-chemical reaction scenario, such as painting a car, the change is physical and not chemical.
 
• This is because the composition of the car has not changed.
